steps: Choose the formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time, Density = Mass ÷ Volume, Pressure = Force ÷ Area.
Check the units match, and convert if needed (km/h to m/s is ÷ 3.6).
Rearrange with a formula triangle: cover the quantity you want to find.
Substitute, calculate, and state the units.
method_card.title: Speed, Density & Pressure
method_card.content:
Each measure is one quantity shared over another. Use a formula triangle: cover the quantity you want. If the other two sit side by side, multiply; if one is above the other, divide.

$$\text{Speed}=\frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}} \quad \text{Density}=\frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} \quad \text{Pressure}=\frac{\text{Force}}{\text{Area}}$$
method_card.example:
A block has mass 450 g and volume 50 cm³.

Density = 450 ÷ 50 = 9 g/cm³.

steps: Break the problem into stages. For average speed over two legs, find each leg's time, then use total distance ÷ total time (never just average the speeds).
For a mixture, add the masses and add the volumes before dividing. For a solid, work out its volume from the shape first, then use the density.
Finish with the rounding the question asks for, and sanity-check the size of your answer.
gold.title: Gold: several steps, then round

steps.label: Check
steps.content: Between 50 and 60, nearer 50 (more time on the slow leg) ✓

example.question: A trip: 100 km at 50 km/h, then 60 km at 60 km/h. Find the average speed (1 d.p.).

steps: Pick the right formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time, Density = Mass ÷ Volume, Pressure = Force ÷ Area. Each is a total shared over how many units.
To find the top quantity, multiply the other two. To find a bottom quantity, divide the top by the one you know. A formula triangle helps: cover what you want.
Do one calculation, then write the units straight from the formula (km ÷ h = km/h).
bronze.title: Bronze: one formula, one step

example.question: A car travels 90 km in 3 hours. Find its speed.

steps: The formula is the same, but first make the pieces fit. You may need to rearrange (Force = Pressure × Area) or convert units before substituting.
km/h to m/s: divide by 3.6. m/s to km/h: multiply by 3.6. kg to g: multiply by 1000. Get the units right, then apply the formula once.
Answers may be decimals. Keep them exact unless the question asks you to round.

guided_steps.hint: The radius squared. Use the radius, not the diameter.
π × r² × h.
Density × volume.

guided_steps.done: Back to 0.6 g/cm³, so 942 g is right.
